meta.mission: Deterministic-first spec extraction for an Apple hardware capability study.
extraction_pipeline: 1. scripts/extract_specs.py attempted a direct script fetch (requests, HTTPS_PROXY-aware, CA bundle /root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt) against apple.com spec/shop pages.

2. Every apple.com and support.apple.com host was rejected at the egress-proxy CONNECT layer with HTTP 403 (organization policy denial, confirmed twice: raw curl/requests via the script, and independently via the WebFetch tool which returned EGRESS_BLOCKED for www.apple.com and support.apple.com). Per proxy policy this was not retried or routed around.

3. Fallback per task step 2: WebSearch (Anthropic-hosted, not subject to this sandbox's egress allowlist) was used to retrieve and synthesize facts from indexed copies of Apple Newsroom / Apple Support pages and corroborating tech press (MacRumors, Macworld, 9to5Mac, AppleInsider, Tom's Hardware/Guide, TechCrunch, Daring Fireball, PetaPixel, ThePCEnthusiast, Technology.org). WebFetch on the underlying press URLs was also attempted for direct-page confirmation but every tested host (apple.com, support.apple.com, appleinsider.com, macworld.com, tomsguide.com, everymac.com, notebookcheck.net) returned EGRESS_BLOCKED, so no raw HTML could be parsed for this study; all figures below come from WebSearch's synthesis of indexed content.

4. Every field below is therefore extraction_method="llm-parse", not "script" -- the script ran successfully but recovered zero fields because its only reachable targets (apple.com) are blocked in this environment. See research/fetch_report.json for the per-URL proxy denial log from the script run.
meta.script_result_summary: 0/8 apple.com targets script-extractable; all failed at proxy CONNECT with 403 (org egress policy), not a parsing failure.
meta.global_extraction_method: llm-parse (WebSearch synthesis of Apple Newsroom/Support content mirrored by tech press, dated 2026-08-25 through 2026-08-28)
meta.verdict_macbook_pro_m5_max: YES. A MacBook Pro with the M5 Max chip exists and is purchasable new from Apple today (2026-08-28). It launched March 3-11, 2026 (Apple Newsroom announcement, pre-orders March 4, availability March 11) in both 14-inch and 16-inch chassis, and remains Apple's current, unsuperseded MacBook Pro flagship as of this study -- it is the best laptop path actually buyable now. Its full max config: 128GB unified memory, up to 614GB/s memory bandwidth (40-core GPU config), up to 8TB SSD, with a fully loaded 16-inch (nano-texture, 128GB, 8TB) configuration reported at $7,349.

machines.memory_bandwidth_note: Reported publicly as '1.2TB/s'; 1229 GB/s used here as the standard binary-GB/s figure for that spec generation, but the exact decimal was not independently re-derived from a primary Apple spec table in this environment (apple.com blocked) -- treat as approximate pending direct confirmation.
machines.price_max_config: 256GB memory, 16TB storage -- this is the highest configuration currently orderable/priced. The true maximum (512GB memory, 16TB storage) is NOT priced yet: 512GB-memory units do not ship until 'late October 2026' and Apple has not published pricing for that tier as of 2026-08-28. Press estimates (based on the $4,000 step from 96GB->256GB and the $7,500 step from 1TB->16TB storage) suggest the full 512GB/16TB config will exceed $20,000, but this is an estimate, not a published price -- do not treat it as verified.
machines.availability: Preorders opened Aug 25, 2026 for configurations up to 256GB memory; ships Sept 22, 2026. The 512GB-memory configuration is announced but not yet orderable/priced -- it ships late October 2026.

machines.storage_note: Base storage doubled to 2TB for this generation; 8TB max reported consistently for the M5 Max tier across both chassis sizes, but the 14-inch-specific top storage SKU was not independently re-confirmed (the confirmed Apple buy-URL for the 128GB/8TB SKU found in search was for the 16-inch chassis).
